newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London focus on firm financials.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London focus on firm financials.

text.p: Firmer financials were most active among Japanese stocks traded here with Nomura leading the way after news of the shake-out among its senior management, dealers said on Tuesday.
At 0105 GMT the Nikkei 50, at 1477.32, was 2.61 points (0.18 percent) up from its opening level.
"It's all been banks and brokers," a trader at a Japanese bank said. "Nomura seem to be putting their house in order and getting the bad news out of the way which has helped them to plus-15 bid."
Nomura Securities were bid at 1,385 yen, up from 1,370 at the Tokyo close after which it announced its president and 15 board members would resign at the end of the month.

Nomura chairman and president Masashi Suzuki said the planned drastic reshuffle in the firm's top management, including his own resignation as president, was aimed at regaining public trust in the brokerage.
In Tokyo trading, the benchmark Nikkei 225 index closed 7.21 points, or 0.04 percent, lower at 18,544.45, ending a five-day winning streak. Volume was 507 million shares.
Brokerages were especially well sought after following rumours about likely developments at Nomura Securities.
